content.text:
Hello, I have problem with my docker setup since two weeks and my colleague also cannot understand it, so maybe you can help me. Sorry if my explanation is not so clear.

The situation is like this. We have small application, is a Python API with a worker and a Postgres, and everything works perfect on my machine and on my colleague machine also. But when we deploy to the server of the customer, the worker container it starts and after maybe 30 seconds it stops, no error message, exit code 0. Not 1, is 0, which I find very strange because for me exit 0 means it finished normally? But it should never finish, it should run forever and wait for jobs.

On the server the docker version is older, is 20.10 something, and on our machines we have 24. I don't know if this is important but I mention it.

This is our compose file, I removed the passwords:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    build: .
    command: uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    depends_on:
      - db
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://app:REDACTED@db:5432/app
      REDIS_URL: redis://cache:6379/0
  worker:
    build: .
    command: celery -A app.worker worker --loglevel=info
    depends_on:
      - db
      - cache
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://app:REDACTED@db:5432/app
      REDIS_URL: redis://cache:6379/0
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
      POSTGRES_DB: app
  cache:
    image: redis:7
volumes:
  pgdata:
```

What we tried already: we added restart: always to the worker, then it restarts in loop forever every 30 seconds which is not better, just more noise in the logs. We tried to run the same command with docker run manually on the server and then it works and stays running, which makes no sense to me because is the same image and same command.

Also when I do docker compose logs worker I see the celery banner and it prints ready, and then nothing, and then the container is gone. There is no traceback anywhere. My colleague thinks is OOM but the server has 16GB and nothing else runs there, and I think if OOM the exit code would be 137 not 0.

Do you have idea what to look for? I am not so experienced with docker so maybe is something obvious that I don't see.
